title: Writing Technical Documentation
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main behavior of writing technical documentation.
Apply writing technical documentation in a small Python example or interpret a representative result.
Identify one limitation, edge case, compatibility concern, or failure mode relevant to the topic.

content.intro: This lesson introduces writing technical documentation as part of professional python development and deployment. It turns the curriculum heading into a short, practical concept guide with a visual, example, and checks to try locally.

content_blocks.title: Version and reliability note
content_blocks.text: Use the interpreter and dependencies declared for your project. Where a feature is version-specific or tool-dependent, check its official documentation and document a useful fallback.

content.task: Try it yourself: adapt the example to demonstrate writing technical documentation with different inputs. Write down your prediction, run it locally, and explain the result plus one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in writing technical documentation without copying the definition.
Run or manually verify the smallest example using the stated runtime assumptions.
Describe one relevant edge case, limitation, or troubleshooting step.
hints: Read the sample carefully and identify the values or state that affect the result.
Change one variable or input at a time and predict what should happen before running it.
Check the official reference and runtime version if behavior differs from the expected result.
